D: An unhappy housewife befriends an elderly woman who tells her the story of two friends who ran a café in 1930s Alabama.
P: Serve the tomatoes when the story arrives at the Whistle Stop Café.
S: Green tomatoes sliced thick, salted 10 minutes, dipped in buttermilk and seasoned cornmeal, fried in bacon fat until golden, with a remoulade.
Idgie takes honey straight from the bee tree for Ruth
Buttermilk biscuits: flour and cold butter cut together, buttermilk folded in, patted, folded three times, cut and baked at 220C for 12 minutes. Warm, with butter and a chunk of honeycomb.

Sharp cheddar mixed with mayo, cream cheese, roasted red capsicum and hot sauce, spread thick on crackers and topped with pickled jalapeno. Grate 250g sharp cheddar. Beat 100g cream cheese with 80g mayo until smooth, then fold in the cheddar, 100g finely chopped roasted red capsicum, a dash of hot sauce, half a tsp smoked paprika and pepper. Chill 30 minutes. Spread thickly on 24 crackers and top each with a slice of pickled jalapeno.
M: the café's barbecue and its famous sauce
Pork shoulder rubbed with paprika, brown sugar and garlic, roasted at 150C for 5 hours, pulled, dressed in a tomato and vinegar sauce. Coleslaw and white bread.

Chicken brined overnight in buttermilk, dredged in peppery seasoned flour and fried crunchy, with garlicky braised greens and warm cornbread. Soak 1.5kg chicken pieces overnight in 500ml buttermilk with 2 tsp salt. Mix 300g flour with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and 2 tsp pepper. Dredge and fry at 165C for 12 to 15 minutes until 74C inside. Wilt 2 bunches kale with garlic and a splash of cider vinegar. Bake cornbread from 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 250ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g butter at 220C for 20 minutes.
W: Toasted pecans, brown sugar, golden syrup, butter and eggs in a blind-baked case, baked at 170C for 50 minutes.
K: Black tea brewed strong with ripe peaches and sugar, chilled and poured over ice with lemon, mint and fresh peach slices. Brew 6 black tea bags in 1L just-boiled water with 2 sliced peaches for 5 minutes. Remove the bags and stir in 100g sugar while hot. Cool completely with the peaches in, then strain. Pour over ice in four tall glasses with lemon slices, fresh peach slices and mint.

s.how: Slice 4 green tomatoes thick and salt for 10 minutes. Dip in 200ml buttermilk, then 150g seasoned cornmeal. Fry in bacon fat from 150g bacon until golden. Mix 100g mayo with chopped capers and lemon for remoulade.

s.note: Idgie takes honey straight from the bee tree for Ruth
s.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 300g flour with 3 tsp baking powder. Fold in 250ml buttermilk, pat out, fold three times, cut and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with butter, honey and a chunk of honeycomb.

m.note: the café's barbecue and its famous sauce
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork shoulder with 1 tbsp paprika, 2 tbsp brown sugar and garlic and roast covered at 150C for 5 hours. Pull and dress with 150ml tomato sauce simmered with 80ml cider vinegar. Serve with slaw and white bread. The secret's in the sauce.

w.how: Blind-bake a tin lined with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust. Whisk 3 eggs, 250ml golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter. Stir in 200g toasted pecans, pour in and bake at 170C for 50 minutes.

d.how: Brew 6 black tea bags in 1L just-boiled water with 2 sliced peaches for 5 minutes. Remove the bags and stir in 100g sugar while hot. Cool completely with the peaches in, then strain. Pour over ice in four tall glasses with lemon slices, fresh peach slices and mint.
